9.4 Lessons

Provenance is the cheapest insurance the schedule can buy. Corrosion has caused fatal pipeline
ruptures where protection and the records behind it failed (Ehstoday 2000), and external corrosion
remains a leading cause of reportable onshore pipeline accidents (Plusstd 2022). The design spends its
first phase making every number traceable before any model consumes it, because an assumed value
that persists silently into a safety computation is the failure both records describe. Calibrate against what
can be measured and envelope what cannot. A rare, short monopolar return will not oblige the schedule
by occurring on cue, and the design says so openly: bipolar baseline for calibration, a conservative
envelope for the monopolar and fault cases, limits stated in the report. A stated limit is defensible; a
hidden one is not. The staffing table is a bid gate, not a formality. Certification is a disqualification trigger
and evaluation marks ride on the certified people as much as on the method, so the personnel are
confirmed and documented before submission rather than assumed into existence afterwards.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Three questions stay open. First, whether a monopolar return occurs during the study window: if one
does, the model gains an event-verified validation case and the envelope assumption can be relaxed; if
not, the envelope stands with its stated limits. Second, whether the 8-inch line's insulating joint recorded
as short at KP-0 is actually shorted: field verification settles it, and the answer changes the boundary
condition the model applies at that joint. Third, whether the four-pin survey resolution is deep enough to
fix the layered soil structure: if it is not, additional borehole resistivity data would be required and the
model's soil regions would be redefined before calibration. Settling each question changes a model input
or a validation claim, which is why each is named now rather than left to surface later.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Intelligence Should Stay with the Pipeline's Owner

The object model, the validation register, the re-runnable model and every compiled record
belong on the operator's own hardware under its own controls, with the public-sector cloud
policy and the absolute-property clause making that the only defensible posture.

Chapter 9 sequenced the work and named its gates. This chapter settles who keeps what the work
produces, and on whose hardware.

10.1 What the Operator Owns, and Where It Sits

The object model, fifteen objects with their typed links, lives in the validation register inside the operator's
own estate, and the contract's absolute-property clause makes every compiled record and every piece of
study software the procuring agency's property, so ownership was never in question; location was. The
register, the discrepancy log and the re-runnable model all sit on one server-class host inside the
operator's facility, consistent with the public-sector cloud policy that binds a federal corporation of this
kind, and no data crosses the estate boundary at any point in the study. The weights carry the smallest
possible burden: no model is trained on the operator's data, the document parser runs as released under
its Apache-2.0 license, and that license places no restriction stopping the operator from holding, rerunning
and archiving the weights on its own hardware indefinitely. There is no fine-tune to govern and no vendor
entitlement to renew. The decision record is the register itself: every provenance value, every
reconciliation and every discrepancy closed by the named Corrosion Control engineer is kept, so the next
decision, whether a future integrity assessment or a mitigation redesign, reads the record instead of
repeating the argument. The boundary is the last owned thing: the reuse bar written into the data
agreement, the handover on media, and the rule that no consultant-side copy survives the handover.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

This design is CodeNinja's work in shape as much as in substance. Hyper Ontology is the object model:
fifteen objects and their typed links turning pipelines, anode beds, electrode stations and assessment
records into one queryable argument. Decision Systems is the reconciliation discipline: provenance,
discrepancy routing and safe-distance recommendations that a named Corrosion Control engineer
accepts or rejects. Sovereign Infrastructure is the hosting posture: the operator's own hardware, an open-
weight Apache-2.0 parser and an in-country estate that nothing leaves. Praxis is the platform that
produced the design, and the chapter that follows traces every choice it made back to what justified it.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

Every Safe Distance Ships With Its Evidence
Corridor Guard is one disciplined argument: scanned records enter through a single adapter into a
provenance-carrying register, corridors are verified in the field before any number is trusted, a calibrated
interference model turns that verified data into safe distances and a priced mitigation strategy, and the
whole chain, parser, register and re-runnable model, stays inside the operator's estate where the
governing clauses already say it belongs.

Running the same shape elsewhere asks for little: a boundary that fixes what data exists, a register that
attaches provenance to every attribute it accepts, field verification before modelling, a calibrated model in
software the industry already validates, and gates that spend data risk early because payment and
credibility both arrive only at the end.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design

Every choice in this paper traces back to recorded reading: this chapter shows the ask as
Praxis framed it, the records in the room, the eight lenses and the patterns adopted and set
aside.

Chapter 10 settled who keeps what the design builds. This closing chapter shows how the design was
reasoned in the first place: what Praxis was given, which lenses it read through and where the reasoning
landed. Every design in the Vertical-Driven Architectures series is produced on CodeNinja Praxis, the
design team platform for designing physical AI systems, and this chapter exists so a reader can trace any
choice in the paper back to what justified it. Figure 9 shows the reasoning in one view: the ask as Praxis
framed it, the records that were in the room, the eight lenses, the patterns adopted and set aside, and the
equipment classes the reasoning landed on.

11.1 The Ask, the Family and What Was in the Room

The ask is a public tender from the Corrosion Control department of an oil and gas operator in Pakistan:
data validation, modelling and a mitigation design against the interference that a high-voltage direct
current transmission system's electrode ground current imposes on the operator's transmission and
distribution gas pipelines. Praxis assigned the design to the Physical AI family and to oil and gas,
because the tender's own subject matter places the work on a Pakistani gas utility's buried pipeline
network, where the physics is electrochemical and the assets are fixed and buried. What was in the room:
1,289 records were listed, 118 were read in full and 1,171 were available on demand. The tender
document itself, its terms of reference, its data annexures and its evaluation schedule were read in full;
the sector precedents and the regulatory record were read as far as the design needed them.

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

The recorded reasoning adopted one pattern and set a family of them aside. The adopted pattern is the
validation-first, gate-exit phase shape: prove the data before the model, and date every gate. The set-

edge model serving, on-site language model serving, object tracking, container orchestration, a model
registry, labelling and retraining, distributed time synchronisation, observability of a running service and a
frontier inference cluster. Each was considered against a stated duty and found to have none: the study
consumes a document package rather than live streams, nothing moves or is tracked, two long-running
workloads share one host, and no model is trained on the operator's data. Setting them aside is itself a
design decision, because each one would have been another thing to hand over inside a fixed schedule.

APPENDIX A

title: Hangar Form Cell: Dieless Robotic Sheet Metal From CAD to Certified Part Without Vendor Cloud
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · AV I AT I O N & A E R O S PA C E M A N U FA C T U R I N G · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S ·
OCTOBER 2026

Hangar Form Cell: Dieless Robotic Sheet
Metal From CAD to Certified Part
Without Vendor Cloud
A vendor-independent dieless robotic sheet metal cell for a United States aircraft
maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) facility that turns CAD into collision-free,
springback-compensated toolpaths with in-process metrology and per-serial traceability,
wholly inside the facility's own boundary.

CodeNinja Engineering Team

For the maintenance lead accountable for structural spare production, hangar superintendents and quality and
compliance leads, and the manufacturing, robotics, controls, metrology and platform engineers who would build and
run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja Atoms series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a
real-world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on CodeNinja Praxis, the CodeNinja
Atoms platform for designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

A Die Should Not Stand Between a Part and Flight
A facility that maintains aircraft needs structural components, brackets, panels, skin sections and spare
parts formed on demand, from CAD to a certified part, without part-specific dies, without long tooling lead
times, and without any vendor cloud touching controlled technical data. It cannot answer that need today
because one-off and low-volume parts depends on heavy, expensive hard tooling that must be designed,
cut, stored and paid for before the first blank is bent, and because the dieless robotic alternatives on the
market arrive with hosted reachback services and software the facility cannot own, which flight-critical
provenance rules will not tolerate.

The design is a dual-arm synchronized dieless cell with generic interchangeable styli, an offline CAD-to-
path and springback compensation stack the facility owns outright, and in-process metrology that closes
the dimensional loop on the facility's own aluminium, steel and titanium sheet. Six source systems enter
through two adapter families into an object model of fourteen objects that carries one Asset Administration
Shell record per serialized part; five services and five surfaces run on the facility's own network, and one
registered model executes at the cell edge. No artifact leaves the boundary, every disposition stays with a
named authorized person, and provenance under the material and cybersecurity rules its contracts flow
down is designed in from the first procurement.

The paper states the facility's problem and its documented cost, then the join failure across the systems
the facility already runs. It fixes the constraints and what the design chose against, lays out the stack from
sources to surfaces, defines the fourteen objects and where the human loop sits, walks the ingestion and
event backbone, places each inference tier with its latency budget, registers the models, hardware
classes and licenses, and plans a three-phase rollout gated by a written kill criterion on sacrificial blanks.
It closes on ownership and on the Praxis chapter that traces every choice back to what justified it.

 Figure 1. Hangar Form Cell on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model, what it computes,
                                            and the person who decides.

Contents

         Sources                                                                   Reference

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

A Spare Part Waits Years for Its Die

Low-volume structural sheet metal at an aircraft maintenance facility is hostage to hard
tooling, and the cost is measured in grounded aircraft, accident findings and supply chains
the facility does not control.

The abstract framed the design in one paragraph: a dieless robotic cell, an offline path-planning stack, in-
process metrology and a per-part record, gated by a written kill criterion. This chapter establishes why
that problem exists at all, what the facility needs to answer it, what the public record says the failure costs,
and what the operation looks like as a working scenario.

1.1 The Question the Facility Needs Answered

The question is narrow and unforgiving: can this structural sheet metal part, for this serial-numbered
aircraft, be formed now on a machine the facility owns, to its drawing tolerance, with evidence a quality
authority will accept, without a die and without a vendor's cloud? The request behind the design asks for
exactly that: structural components, brackets, panels, skin sections and spare parts at heavy
maintenance, line maintenance and factory level, produced from CAD to collision-free toolpath with
springback compensation and in-process measurement.

Answering it requires data the facility already holds or can generate in the cell: the CAD model with its
revision and tolerance callouts; the blank pedigree, meaning alloy, temper, thickness, mill certificate and
lot number; the arm calibration state and encoder health; the force trace of every pass; the deviation map
of every scan against CAD; the work order that names the aircraft; and the quality record that carries any
nonconformance to disposition. The regulatory ground is equally specific. Camera imagery and process
data on export-controlled parts are controlled technical data under the export control regulations (ITAR
and the EAR); the controlled information the operator's contracts flag is governed by the NIST SP 800-
171 security controls those contracts require; specialty metals provenance binds under the material
provenance clauses the operator's customers flow down; record-keeping duties for parts follow 14 CFR
21.137; and the cell itself must satisfy ISO 10218 to 1:2025 robot safety, 29 CFR 1910.212 machine
guarding and 1910.147 lockout and tagout.

1.2 What the Failure Costs

Hard tooling is the reason the question goes unanswered. Dies and presses carry long lead times, high
upfront cost and permanent physical storage, so a low-volume structural part waits for its die or waits for a
supply chain the facility does not control. The documented cost of a maintenance enterprise stretched
past its ability to produce and verify parts is not hypothetical. An investigation into a 2017 crash that killed
16 blamed consistent production errors at the maintenance complex where the aircraft had undergone
maintenance (WJCL 2017). An accident report into the death of a technician working on an aircraft found
the death was caused by multiple points of failure (Militarytimes 2024). One large aircraft operator's own
fiscal year summary of its most serious aviation accident class lists annual counts for manned aviation
ranging from 1 to 23 (AF 2024). None of these findings trace to a single missing die. Together they
describe what a maintenance facility looks like when parts, processes and evidence are scarce: schedule
pressure, workarounds, and the kind of compounded failures that accident boards then reconstruct.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The scenario is one aircraft maintenance facility running one dieless cell beside its existing capability. The
cell holds two synchronized robotic arms with generic, interchangeable styli inside an interlocked
enclosure, a sheet loading station, a metrology bay with a structured-light scanner and a laser tracker
reference channel, and its own compute, running wholly in-country on the facility's power with no external
link. The work is low-volume and high-mix: one-off spares on demand, formed panels on the order of two

meters, brackets and skin sections in aluminium first, with steel and titanium investigated as a measured
extension. Five roles stand in the loop: facility operators who load, run and inspect; process programmers
who release toolpaths; cell maintainers who track stylus wear and calibration; quality personnel who hold
first article inspection and material review evidence; and an accountable production lead. The
environments are a shop floor with thermal drift, dust and temperature swings, and a controlled room for
the record layer. The design counts are fixed: five named source systems, two adapter families, fourteen
objects, five services, five surfaces, one registered model, three phases and four tracked requirements.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Every Facility System Sees One Slice of the Part

CAD, the robot controller, the metrology bay, the work order system and the quality records
each hold one fragment of a formed part, and none of them together can prove the part
conforming.

Chapter 1 established the question and the regulatory ground. This chapter shows why the facility cannot
answer that question today: each of its systems holds one fragment of a formed part, and the fragments
have never been joined. Figure 2 sets the slices side by side.

2.1 What Each System Sees and What It Misses

The CAD import carries the geometry, its revision and the tolerance callouts, but it knows nothing of the
metal: it cannot say whether any formed part matches the drawing, or what the process did to get there.
The robot controller sees axis positions, joint torques and the force applied by the stylus, pass by pass,
yet it holds no part identity, no blank pedigree and no dimensional verdict; a flawless force signature on
the wrong lot is invisible to it. The metrology bay produces a deviation map of the scanned surface
against CAD with the instrument's calibration state attached, but the scan arrives orphaned: the force
history, the blank lot and the toolpath version behind that piece of metal live elsewhere. The production
system sees the work order, the aircraft, the due date and the priority, and none of the physical state of
the part or any measurement taken on it. The quality records system files nonconformances, dispositions
and first article evidence, but it receives them after the fact; the live in-process measurements that would
prove conformity before inspection never reach it.

      Figure 2. Five systems, each seeing one part of the answer. the question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

What no system sees is the argument. To prove a serialized part conforming, someone must join the
drawing revision the geometry came from, the certified blank it was cut from, the force signature of every
pass against its baseline, the deviation map against tolerance with the instrument's calibration state at the
moment of scan, and the named person who dispositioned any departure. Today that join is assembled by
hand, after the fact, from exports and paperwork. The cost in practice is measured in repeated first article
work, material review queues that hold parts nobody can prove, and the specific hazard the design is built
to close: a disturbed part with no record is an event nobody notices until it matters.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Four Constraints Shape the Cell

No vendor cloud, owned artifacts, per-serial traceability and a cheap first gate fix every
downstream choice from arm pairing to license selection.

Chapter 2 showed that the join failure is not a missing system but a missing connection, and that buying a
larger single system would not close it. Four constraints fix the shape of the connection instead, and each
one eliminates whole families of downstream choices before any component is named.

3.1 No Vendor Cloud and No Reachback

The first constraint is that the cell runs wholly offline on the facility's local network, on hardware the facility
owns, inside the United States by the operator's own requirement. This is hard here because aerospace
manufacturing software defaults to vendor-hosted services, and because export control makes camera
imagery and process data on controlled parts controlled technical data, which means every byte the cell
produces is data whose location is a compliance question. The NIST SP 800-171 controls the operator's
contracts require govern the controlled information the request itself flags. A hosted assistive service,
however convenient, would put controlled technical data outside the perimeter, so the design offers no
reachback path at all.

3.2 The Facility Owns Every Artifact

The second constraint is ownership of the stack: weights, trained detectors, toolpath baselines, the record
layer and every container image, held by the facility. This is hard because industrial software is licensed
rather than owned, and because specialty metals provenance under the clauses the operator's customers
flow down must be evidenced per item, which the design answers by registering every item before
procurement rather than after delivery. Choosing the Apache-2.0 licensed anomaly detector and the open-
source Apache line for streaming keeps the bill of materials fully owned by the operator, with no
subscription sitting inside a sovereign perimeter.

3.3 Traceability Per Serialized Part

The third constraint is that the record attaches to the serialized part instance, never the part type. This is
hard because maintenance traceability tools traditionally record part numbers, and because 14 CFR
21.137 quality-system duties and flight-critical practice demand an evidence trail per instance: which
certified blank, which program version, which scans, which disposition by which authorized person. Every
formed part carries its own Asset Administration Shell record, and the system prepares evidence while the
disposition itself remains an airworthiness judgement by a named person, never a system output.

3.4 A First Gate That Can Stop the Work Cheaply

The fourth constraint is that the riskiest assumption is tested first, in metal, on the facility's own
aluminium, with a written kill criterion in the facility's own numbers before any flight part is attempted. This
is hard because robotics programs are typically justified as full production commitments, and because the
sector carries a specific warning: a previous industry attempt at automated fuselage assembly was
abandoned after dual-arm synchronization proved unreliable on large flexible panels. Phase one
therefore spends its twelve items on sacrificial blanks, synchronization and springback convergence, so
that if the physics refuses, the work stops at prototype cost.

3.5 Scoping Decisions

The constraints resolve into three scoping decisions, each bought at a stated price, as Table 1 records.

3.6 What the Design Chose Against

Each rejection follows from a constraint rather than from preference, as Table 2 records, ending with what
sits outside the scope entirely.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 4

One Stack Runs From CAD to the Cell

A layered architecture puts systems of record below, one object model in the middle, and the
path, metrology and governance services above it.

Chapter 3 fixed the constraints: the cell runs wholly offline inside a sovereign perimeter, the facility owns
every artifact it produces, compliance controls are engineered from the first procurement, and the riskiest
assumption is spent on sacrificial metal first. This chapter shows the stack those constraints produced,
layer by layer.

4.1 Three Bands, One Object Model

The architecture is three bands with one contract between them. At the bottom sit the systems of record:
CAD import, the production systems, the quality records system, and the cell's own control layer. They
already hold the engineering truth, and the design replaces none of them; it reads them. In the middle sits
one object model: fourteen objects held as Asset Administration Shells in Eclipse BaSyx, an international
standard for a machine-readable asset record, where the slices are joined into a single record per
serialized part. Above it run five services that do the work and five surfaces where named people see
state and decide. Figure 3 shows the layers with their counts: six source systems, two adapter families,
fourteen objects, five services, five surfaces and one registered model.

The contract between the bands is the reason the shape fits this industry. Flight-critical manufacturing
demands that every judgement about a part be attributable and reproducible, so every write into the
model travels through a service that stamps the acting person, the time and the provenance onto the
event. A document store per application cannot give that guarantee, because each copy of a part record
drifts from its source. Sovereignty is enforced by placement rather than by policy: K3s orchestrates
containers on facility hardware, the Harbor registry holds images and the registered model behind an air
gap, Prometheus, Grafana and Loki observe the running system inside the perimeter, and Keycloak holds
identity. A hardware data diode governs the only egress from the cell's operational technology zone, so
monitoring leaves one way and nothing returns.

A single event shows the flow. A structured-light scan of a formed panel is acquired at the metrology bay,
timestamped by the site grandmaster clock, carried by the telemetry adapter onto the event backbone,
written into the scan object against the part it evaluated, judged by the metrology and quality service, and
raised on the formed-part record and first article inspection evidence queue if it falls outside tolerance. No
stage touches a source system directly, and no surface writes to the model except through its service.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 5

Fourteen Objects Turn Shop Data Into Traceability

The object model links every blank, scan, force trace, toolpath release and nonconformance
to one serialized part, and the only write path runs through a named person.

Chapter 4 placed one object model at the center of the stack and promised that a query could cross it.
This chapter opens the model: its fourteen objects, the typed links between them, the human loop, and
the hosting posture that keeps the record sovereign.

5.1 Fourteen Objects and Their Typed Links

The focal object is the formed structural part. It carries the part number, the serial number, the alloy and
temper, the sheet thickness, the as-built deviation to CAD and a formability verdict, and its status
vocabulary runs from Blank staged through In-process scan and Final scan to Conforming,
Nonconforming and MRB dispositioned, where MRB is the material review board, the authorized body
that dispositions a nonconforming flight-critical part.

Around it, the model holds what the part is made from and where: the sheet blank with its mill certificate
reference and lot number, the dieless cell with its work envelope and enclosure state, the robot arms with
calibration and encoder health, and the styli with wear counts and assignments. It holds what defines the
part: the part CAD model with revision and tolerance callouts, the formability analysis with predicted
thinning and springback, and the program whose toolpath version and springback compensation passes
were released. It holds what measures the part: the in-process metrology scan with its deviation map and
calibration state, and the force trace with peak load and signature residual. And it holds the accountability
frame: the work order, the nonconformance with its evidence pack, the facility operator, and the cell model
service with its weights hash and release state.

Figure 4 draws the objects and their typed links. The reach is the point: from one serial number, a query
follows links to the mill certificate behind the blank, the CAD revision the toolpath was cut from, each
scan's deviation map and the calibration state of the instrument that took it, the force traces of every pass,
the operator who released the program, the work order's aircraft, and any nonconformance with its
evidence pack. A document store keeps one record per part and can reach none of that without copying
it; here the links are typed, so the first article inspection pack is assembled by traversal rather than by
hand. The record earns its keep on the day a process error is found: an investigation into a 2017 crash
that killed 16 blamed consistent production errors at the maintenance complex that had serviced the
aircraft (WJCL 2017), and a traversable record is what lets a facility find every affected serial the same
day.

          Figure 4. The fourteen objects of the model and the typed links that let a query reach across them.

5.2 The Human Loop and the Hosting Posture

The human loop lives at three points, and all three are decisions the system prepares but never takes. A
program moves from Draft to Released only on the action of a named facility operator. A scan moves to
Conforming or Out of tolerance on the metrology service's verdict, but a nonconforming part reaches
MRB dispositioned only through an authorized person's disposition, with the evidence pack attached. The
model's only write path runs through its five services; the adapters and the event backbone are read-only
toward sources, and every write carries the acting person and the timestamp.

The hosting posture follows the same rule. Everything runs on facility infrastructure inside the United
States, under the facility's own identity in Keycloak with a named account per person; there are no
external links, and controlled technical data never crosses the boundary. The cell model service is the one
object that changes underneath the work, so it carries its own governance: a weights hash, thresholds,
and a release state of Released, Shadow, Superseded or Rolled back, changed only through the model
and baseline governance queue.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter

Six source systems reach the object model through two adapter families and an ordered
event backbone, so provenance is fixed at the door rather than argued later.

Chapter 5 defined the model that holds the record. This chapter defines the door: which sources enter it,
what the adapters guarantee before anything is written, and how the backbone orders it all.

6.1 Six Sources and Their Provenance Classes

Six source systems reach the model, and each enters with its provenance class stamped at the door.
Three are operator-held, meaning the interface exists at the operator and is described in its own
requirement: CAD import in STEP and IGES, the operator's own sensors, and third-party software
interfaces with the auxiliary metrology equipment the requirement calls for. Two are domain-typical,
meaning every facility of this kind runs them but the requirement names no product, so the exact interface
is confirmed at the first facility: the production systems that carry work orders and aircraft context, and the
quality records system that must receive nonconformance and first article inspection evidence. The sixth
is cell control telemetry, the robot controllers, load cells and safety PLC read through MTConnect, which
is operator-held because it belongs to the cell the design builds. Figure 5 maps each system to its class
and its adapter path.

         Figure 5. The 6 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

The adapter tier, two families wide, makes guarantees that hold no matter which source sits behind it.
Every payload enters through the integration adapter, which carries documents, orders and records, or
the telemetry adapter, which carries machine and sensor streams; nothing reaches the object model
directly. Provenance is fixed at ingress, so a record's origin is never argued later. The adapters are read-
only toward sources and never write back to a system of record. Schema and unit validation reject
malformed payloads to a dead-letter path rather than passing them downstream. Idempotency keys mean
a replayed scan cannot be counted twice. And calibration state travels with every metrology payload, so a
measurement taken with an out-of-calibration instrument is flagged at the door rather than discovered at
audit.

6.3 The Event Backbone

The backbone is Apache Kafka 4.3 in KRaft mode, the Kafka line that carries its own consensus and
removes the separate coordination service, self-managed inside the perimeter, which keeps the bill of
materials fully owned by the operator. Ordering is by partition keyed on the part serial, so every event for
one serialized part arrives in sequence no matter which source raised it.

Delivery is at least once with idempotent consumers, so a redelivered event changes nothing. Buffering
absorbs the bursts that forming produces: the scan, its force trace and the camera metadata for one pass
arrive together, and the backbone holds them until services drain the queue. Replication runs across
broker nodes on site only; there is no off-site replication, because nothing leaves the boundary.

Time is the quiet guarantee underneath. An OCP Time Card grandmaster with linuxptp and chrony keeps
every hop on one clock, so a force trace, a scan and a video frame pass order correctly when the model
joins them. Without that shared clock, a joined record is a guess with a timestamp attached.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

Detection Runs at the Cell, Reasoning In-Facility

Vision and force anomaly detection execute on the cell edge box inside the safety cycle,
while model governance and compensation baselines stay on a facility server behind the
facility's own controls.

Chapter 6 brought every stream into the object model through its adapter family, with ordering guaranteed
at the backbone. This chapter places the computation that turns those streams into verdicts: what runs on
the cell floor, what stays on the facility server, and what each failure of link, power or update path leaves
standing.

7.1 Two Tiers of Inference, Each with a Different Job

Figure 6 places inference in two tiers. The first is a fanless industrial inference computer mounted in the
cell panel, chosen for shop-floor temperature and dust rather than for any single model, and sized from
the camera and sensor stream budget with headroom; its final capacity is bench-measured on the actual
streams before the order is placed. This box serves the Anomalib 2.7.0 vision detectors and the force-
trace residual checks through ONNX Runtime, so surface and geometric anomaly detection on in-process
and post-form scans executes inside the cell's own rhythm, interleaved between passes. It sits there for
two reasons: a flagged pass must be caught before the next pass begins, and the certified safety
argument requires the cell to stand on its own hardware without reaching across the plant for a verdict.

The second tier is an air-cooled facility server of the eight-card 48 GB PCIe inference class, running on
the facility's own power. It holds the registered model estate with KV and batch headroom, the thresholds
that turn a detection into a hold, and the versioned springback compensation baselines; the cell model
service governs each release through its states of released, shadow, superseded and rolled back, with
retraining data prepared in CVAT and Label Studio and artifacts held in Harbor. No language model role is
committed, so no frontier cluster is sized; if an agentic work surface is confirmed later, a US-hosted node
class would be sized against this register then. On memory arithmetic, the design sizes from what is
known: anomaly detectors at FP32 typically occupy tens to hundreds of megabytes, and memory-bank
methods such as PatchCore grow with the number of reference images, so the detector footprint is fixed
on the chosen model before the card count is finalized. Event ordering across both tiers rides an OCP
Time Card grandmaster with linuxptp, giving sub-millisecond agreement so a scan, its force trace and the
arm pose that produced it share one clock.

           Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 The Latency Budget Follows the Safety Cycle

The budget's spine is non-interference. The certified safety function, the light curtains, safety PLC and
interlocks, owns stopping and admits no software verdict as a control input. Around it the design carries
three advisory budgets: detection must complete within the pause between passes so a flagged pass
stops before the next begins; scan evaluation must complete between acquisition at the metrology bay
and the deviation map to CAD reaching the record; and alert routing must land in the escalation queue
while the part is still on the fixture. Every hop that must order events carries PTP hardware timestamping,
and time-sensitive networking is named only if the bench shows bounded latency is genuinely needed.
Each budget is verified against bench-measured streams, not asserted on paper.

7.3 What Crosses the Boundary, and What Each Failure Leaves Standing

One thing crosses the boundary, and it crosses one way: lidi and Eurydice carry scan records, force
traces, detection events and calibration and stylus wear state over a hardware data diode from the cell
OT zone to the facility tier. Nothing flows back over the diode. Released programs reach the cell through
the signed, scheduled release path in the registry, never as a return channel. The failure paths are
designed explicitly because a published accident report traced a maintenance death to multiple points of
failure rather than a single one (Militarytimes 2024). If the link fails, the cell keeps forming, edge detection
continues, and records queue until the diode path returns. If power fails, Network UPS Tools signals a
clean shutdown, and the safety PLC and interlocks stand on a power path apart from the compute. If an
update fails, Harbor still holds the last released artifact set and the model service rolls back; a stuck
release degrades the system to its last released state, never to an unversioned one.

The License Decides What the Facility Can Own

An Apache-2.0 anomaly detector, open reference architectures and an open streaming
backbone keep every weight, threshold and artifact owned by the operator inside the
perimeter.

Chapter 7 fixed where inference runs and what crosses between tiers. This chapter fixes what runs there,
and why every weight, threshold and artifact that touches a flight-critical part can be owned by the facility
outright. Figure 7 shows the model stack in one view: two edge models behind one serving runtime, one
governance service above them, and the registry and release queue that decide what the cell is allowed
to run. Every entry in it is open weight or open source, and every one was checked against the exclusion
that bars software from covered-nation publishers regardless of its license.

                       Figure 7. The one model, their placement, and the work each one does.

8.1 Anomaly Detection on the Facility's Own Good Parts

The committed vision model is Anomalib 2.7.0, an open library of unsupervised anomaly detection
methods for industrial imagery. Its role is surface and geometric anomaly detection on in-process and
post-form scans of formed panels, placed on the cell edge box and served through ONNX Runtime at
FP32 precision. Its footprint is model dependent, typically tens to hundreds of megabytes, and memory-
bank methods such as PatchCore also grow with the number of reference images, so the final size is
fixed on the chosen variant before the compute box is ordered. The license is Apache-2.0: permissive,
with no copyleft obligation and no field-of-use restriction, which is precisely what permits the facility to
hold, retrain and redistribute the trained detector as its own property. It was chosen because an
unsupervised fit on the facility's own good panels needs no labeled defect set at stand-up, and over the
D-FINE closed-set detector family because a formed panel's deviations are open-ended rather than a
fixed class list.

Beside it, Chronos-Bolt carries the force-feedback load anomaly baselines, learning what a healthy pass
looks like on each arm and stylus combination and flagging signatures that drift. It is also Apache-2.0 and
also runs on the edge box. Both models were named from the catalog and checked live against the
covered-nation exclusion before entering the register.

8.2 Ownership Is a License Question, and the Perimeter Enforces It

The same logic runs through the rest of the stack. Apache Kafka 4.3 is self-managed in KRaft mode on
the open Apache line rather than on a commercial platform subscription, keeping the bill of materials fully
owned by the operator. The two patterns the design stands on, an on-premises AI platform reference
architecture and a simulation-first robotics reference architecture, are adopted as documented
architectures the facility implements on its own hardware, not as subscriptions. BaSyx, InfluxDB 3 Core,
Harbor and Keycloak are open, so no artifact in the traceability chain sits behind a foreign dependency or
a vendor cloud. The capability request requires the cell to run wholly offline on the local network, and the
stack honors that by construction. The stakes are not abstract: a 2017 crash that killed 16 was blamed on
consistent production errors at an aircraft maintenance complex (WJCL 2017), and the evidence pack,
from mill certificate to disposition, is what the quality system reads. Evidence the facility cannot own is
evidence it cannot answer for.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 9

Shadow Mode Comes Before Any Flight Part

Three phases prove arm synchronization and springback convergence on sacrificial blanks
under a written kill criterion before a single flight-critical part is formed.

Chapter 8 closed the model register with a single anomaly detector, Apache-2.0, running on the edge box
inside the cell perimeter, and with no language model committed until the work surface question is settled
by the issuer. This chapter turns the design into a sequence of three phases whose gates let the facility

stop work cheaply, beginning with the riskiest assumption of all: that two robot arms holding generic styli
can form a large, flexible panel to aircraft tolerance.

9.1 Three Phases and Their Exit Gates

Phase one, the validation prototype, carries 12 items across four workstreams: forming cell hardware,
CAD-to-Path software, compliance and supply chain, and metrology and quality. Its items include the cell
site survey and footprint definition, the dual-arm synchronized station build, and the offline CAD-to-Path
workbench with formability analysis. Its exit gate is a written kill criterion, stated in the facility's own
numbers for arm synchronization reliability and springback convergence, tested on sacrificial aluminium
blanks in simulation first and then in metal. If the numbers miss the criterion, the work stops there, before
any flight-critical part is attempted. Phase two, the production cell, carries 5 items across three
workstreams: CAD-to-Path software, rollout and training, and metrology and quality. Its items are the in-
process metrology loop with force feedback and scanning, the formed-part digital record with
airworthiness traceability, and the surface and force anomaly detection services. Its exit gate is operator
training and independent operation certification, meaning facility staff run the cell and its record layer on
their own authority. Phase three, the materials extension, carries 1 item, a steel and titanium limit
investigation under the metrology and quality workstream, and its gate is a measured limits report that
quotes achievable accuracy as a range before any production claim for those alloys is made. Figure 8
shows the three phases, their item counts, workstreams, gates and requirement coverage together: the
four stated requirements of the request for information are covered, with none partial and none left open.

             Figure 8. The three phases and their gates, and coverage of the 4 requirements across them.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The rollout measures five things on every formed panel: the number of springback compensation passes
needed to reach tolerance, the as-built deviation to CAD at each pass, the load signature residual pass,
the conformity rate of in-process scans against their calibration state, and the temperature of the cell
frame and fixture recorded beside every measurement. It also measures the record layer itself: every
disturbed part must carry a record, and a part without one is an event the system raises. The sector's

safety history is the reason the interlock and lockout states sit inside the measured set rather than outside
it: a crash investigation once blamed consistent production errors at an aircraft maintenance complex for
the loss of an aircraft and its crew (WJCL 2017), and a technician's death in a maintenance workplace
was attributed to multiple points of failure rather than one (Militarytimes 2024).

9.4 Lessons

Shadow the flags before anyone trusts them. The anomaly detector runs in shadow against live scans
until its false alarm rate on the facility's own panels is known, and only then does an out-of-tolerance
verdict from it hold a part in the escalation queue. An alert stream that pages the floor faster than people
can act destroys the record layer it is meant to protect, so the alert budget is set before the detector is

promoted. Register provenance before procurement, not after delivery. Specialty metals and prohibited-
source rules bite hardest when they surface late, so registration of every item precedes the purchase
order, and substitutions are identified while alternatives still exist. Treat accreditation as engineering, not
paperwork. The controls the boundary demands shape the network diagram, the camera plan and the
record retention path, so the accreditation workstream sits beside the station build in phase one rather
than behind it.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Three questions remain open. First, whether springback convergence holds across the full range of
geometries the facility intends to form: settling it converts the phase one accuracy range into a firm per-
alloy figure and widens the part family the cell can accept. Second, whether technicians and engineers
will build agents around path planning and springback compensation, which the issuer has not confirmed:
settling it would add the agentic work surface and a serving role for a language model that the register
currently holds open. Third, whether the steel and titanium limits measured in phase three support
production claims or only repair work: settling it decides whether the cell's duty extends beyond
aluminium skins and brackets into primary structure.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Toolpaths and Traceability Stay with the Facility

The object model, the trained detector, the decision record and the security boundary are
held by the facility, with the platform partner named once at the end.

Chapter 9 left three questions open and set the gates that resolve them. This chapter states who holds
what the design builds, because a cell that must run without vendor cloud or vendor reachback is only
sovereign if the artifacts themselves sit in the facility's hands.

10.1 What the Facility Holds

The object model is the facility's: 14 objects with their typed links and status vocabularies are defined in
the facility's own instance, exportable in open formats, and every adapter writes into it rather than into a
vendor tenant. The weights are the facility's: the anomaly detector carries an Apache-2.0 license, so the
trained detector and any fine-tune against the facility's own good panels are owned outright, and the cell
model service object records the weights hash, thresholds and release state so any superseded or rolled-
back model is identifiable. The decision record is the facility's: released toolpath programs with their CAD
revision and compensation pass count, nonconformance dispositions with their authorized person and
evidence pack, and springback baseline versions all live in the facility's quality system of record, where a
flight-critical disposition can be audited; the system prepares the evidence and the named person makes
the airworthiness judgment. The boundary is the facility's: the cell runs inside an air-gapped operational

zone, egress crosses a hardware data diode one way only, identity is administered locally, and the
controlled information handling follows the security controls the facility's contracts already require.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

The design was produced on CodeNinja Praxis, the CodeNinja Atoms platform for designing physical AI
systems, and maps to CodeNinja's offer as follows: Adaptive Operations covers the sensing, detection
and forecasting of physical behavior, from the force traces and joint telemetry to the surface and
geometric anomaly detection on formed panels; Decision Systems covers the ranking, attribution and
reconciliation that a named person decides, holding parts in the escalation queue and preparing
nonconformance evidence for the authorized disposition; Hyper Ontology is the 14-object model that joins
blank, arm, stylus, program, scan and work order into one traceable argument; and Sovereign
Infrastructure is the air-gapped, in-country operation on the facility's own hardware, with open licenses the
operator can own. CodeNinja builds and runs systems of this shape with the operators who own the
problem.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

One Cell Pattern Forms in Any Hangar
In one view the design is a dieless robotic sheet metal cell the facility owns outright: dual-arm
synchronized with generic styli, an offline CAD-to-path and springback compensation stack with versioned
baselines, in-process metrology closing the loop through force traces and structured-light scans, and
fourteen objects carrying a per-serialized-part record that joins blank certificate, formability verdict,
toolpath release and nonconformance evidence into one argument, all running inside the facility's security
boundary with no external service and every airworthiness disposition left to a named authorized person.

The same shape runs in any heavy maintenance, line maintenance or factory facility that forms low-
volume sheet metal: hold the record per serialized instance rather than part type, validate the riskiest
physical assumption on sacrificial material before any flight part moves, keep every toolpath, weight and
scan inside the operator's own boundary on open licenses it can hold, treat accreditation and the safety
case as first-phase engineering rather than later paperwork, and gate each new alloy or geometry on
measured limits before any production claim.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design

Every choice in the paper traces back to recorded reading: the ask, the lens table, the
patterns adopted and set aside, and the equipment classes the reasoning landed on.

Chapter 10 placed the object model, the weights, the decision record and the boundary in the facility's
hands, with the platform partner named once. This last chapter shows how the design itself was
produced, so that any reader can trace a choice in the paper back to what justified it. Every design in this
series is produced on CodeNinja Praxis, and Figure 9 shows how this one was reasoned: the ask as
stated, the family and industry assigned, the records in the room, the eight lenses consulted, the patterns
adopted, and the equipment classes the reasoning landed on. Nothing in the chapters above stands
without a line in that figure.

11.1 Contextualizing the Ask

The ask, in the operator's own words, was dieless robotic sheet metal of aircraft aluminium, steel and
titanium parts, from CAD to collision-free toolpaths with springback compensation and in-process
measurement, with no vendor cloud, deploying in the United States. Praxis assigned the design to the
Physical AI family and to aviation and aerospace manufacturing, because the operator's own words place
the work at heavy maintenance, line maintenance and factory level facilities: structural components,
brackets, panels and skin sections. What was in the room: 981 records were listed, 126 were read in full,
and 855 are available on demand, including the capability request itself, robotics and maintenance
automation precedents, the rules instruments, and the hardware and tooling catalogs.

Two patterns were adopted. The on-premises AI platform pattern is primary: because the ask fixes

as two layers under a clean contract, models served through standard interfaces, and reference
workloads validated before handoff. The robotics simulation pattern is supporting: collision-free toolpaths
and dimensional tolerance must be proven before metal is cut, so every asset is converted to OpenUSD
once, physics and sensors are applied in simulation, and path validation runs software-in-the-loop before
any blank is loaded. No pattern was set aside: the shelf held nothing the design took up and then
rejected, because the constraints in Chapter 3 had already removed the alternatives that such a list would
hold.

vision and time-series models with headroom and needs no frontier node because no language model

event ordering across sensors and controllers; the hardware data diode with its one-way transfer software

keeps the cell clean, mounted and powered on shop-floor supply. Each class is a sizing rule rather than a

closing point of the chapter and of the paper: every lens citation, every pattern, every object and every

title: Turbine Island Watch: Condition Monitoring and Diagnostics for a Combined Cycle Plant in Pakistan
text:
Turbine Island Watch: Condition
ENERGY & UTILITIES · SYSTEM DESIGN

Monitoring and Diagnostics for a
Combined Cycle Plant in Pakistan
We designed a steam turbine condition monitoring system for a rehabilitated 280 MW
turbine-generator at a combined cycle plant in Pakistan. The platform reads the DCS,
the vibration rack and the generator protection systems through a one-way path,
ranks anomalies into prescribed actions, and runs entirely on the operator's own
hardware. This post explains it mechanism by mechanism.
CodeNinja Engineering Team, Forward Deployed Engineering 2026-10-14 19 min read 4,473 words
14 figures

Introduction

STG-1 sits inside a combined cycle plant, feeding a 280 MW steam turbine generator cooled by hydrogen at
20 kV, protected by a rehabilitated 3500 vibration monitoring rack on the turbine bearings, and operated from
a shift desk where process, alarm and vibration context arrive through the plant's distributed control system.
When a bearing housing runs at its nominal 2.3 mm/s RMS, the protection layer is quiet and the shift
operator's attention is elsewhere. An industry analysis of steam turbine condition monitoring puts the cost of
a single unplanned outage at more than half a million dollars per incident, which is the arithmetic that makes
bearing vibration worth watching continuously rather than at the trip threshold of 6.21 mm/s RMS in Zone C.
We set out to design a steam turbine condition monitoring system and a power plant predictive maintenance
platform around that rehabilitated machine, for a grid-connected generation company in Pakistan. The
constraints were fixed before we started. Every tier runs on the operator's own hardware inside the plant
perimeter, because Pakistan has no hyperscaler region and no managed cloud is assumed anywhere. The
NEPRA Security of IT and OT Regulations 2022 bind the design to domain separation, least privilege and five
years of tamper-evident logs. The platform reads the upgraded DCS and never writes to it, the existing trip
philosophy is preserved, and the models are pretrained open weights requiring no training run. The plant sits
roughly 600 km from the port, so spares and model updates arrive on the site's own import cycle, and the
design treats that as a constraint rather than an afterthought.
This blog describes the operation as an engineer who has never seen the plant needs to see it, the technical
problem the existing instrumentation cannot solve alone, the layered architecture from surfaces to sources,
the ontology of 10 objects that grounds every alert, the ingestion path through 4 adapter families from 8
named systems, the inference workflow from vibration reading to severity-ranked alert to condition work
order, the two open-weight models and why each was chosen, and the delivery phases with the gates the
design sets for itself.

Background: how this operation runs
The plant is a combined cycle site. Steam turbine STG-1 is under rehabilitation, together with its foundation
and allied equipment, and the rehabilitation delivers a new steam turbine generator rated 280 MW at 20 kV,
hydrogen-cooled, connected through an SF6 generator circuit breaker at 23 kV and an isolated phase busbar
rated 20 kV and 10000 A. Main and auxiliary transformers carry the output to the switchyard. Gas turbines
GT-1 and GT-2 continue in simple cycle, undisturbed by the works. The vibration instrumentation is a 3500
rack on the STG-1 and STG bearings, and fire detection instruments cover the turbine bearing areas to NFPA
850. Hydrogen leakage detectors and a rotor winding short-circuit on-line detection device come with the
new generator.
The people are the employer's operational personnel, led on the floor by the shift operator, and the
contractor's warranty engineer, who carries defect liability period obligations and reviews evidence through
the contract's document management system. Monthly reporting reconciles against the Primavera P6
programme that governs the contract schedule. Field crews work in the plant's maintenance system of

record, a plant CMMS or EAM that is domain-typical rather than named in the requirement, and which the
design treats as to be confirmed.
The systems already running are the upgraded DCS delivered under the EPC, the rehabilitated 3500 rack, the
generator condition monitoring systems, and the contract DCS and document systems of record. Five
cameras watch the site: wide views over the plant switchyard and the STG-1 island transformer yard, close
views of the electronic room DCS cabinet and the switchyard permit-to-work barrier line, and a control view
over the STG-1 shift operator desk. Figure 1 shows the customer's world and the platform's boundary, with 8
named systems feeding it, 4 roles working it, and 7 of the 10 places the plan staged sitting under it. Figure 2
shows the simulation at steady state drawn on the site's own terrain, every staged asset watched
continuously, with STG-1 bearing housing vibration running at its nominal 2.3 mm/s RMS.

Figure 1:    The customer's world and the platform's boundary: 8 named systems feed it, 4 roles work it, 7 of
the 10 places the plan staged sit under it.

Figure 2:  The simulation at steady state, drawn on the site's own terrain: every asset the plan staged,
watched continuously, with st-16 bearing housing vibration running at its nominal.

The problem
Each existing system answers a narrow question, and none of them answers the question that matters. The
upgraded DCS holds process, alarm and vibration context, but its alarm philosophy is built around the existing
trip logic, so it speaks when the machine is already lost. The 3500 rack measures bearing vibration channels
on STG-1 and the STG bearings, which makes it the primary instrument for the bearing failure modes the plant
cares about, yet a rack delivers channels, not diagnoses, and its protection role ends at the Zone C trip. The
generator's rotor winding short-circuit on-line detection device and the hydrogen leakage detectors each
watch one fault class in isolation. Rotor winding fault detection works by sensing the electrical signature of
inter-turn shorts on line, and hydrogen leakage detection works by gas sensing around the generator casing,
but neither reading is correlated with bearing vibration or process conditions anywhere in the current stack.
What no system sees together is the trajectory. A bearing that trends from 2.3 mm/s RMS toward the 6.21
mm/s RMS Zone C boundary passes through weeks of readable evidence, and none of the present
instruments assemble that evidence into a single, unit-checked history per channel. Threshold tuning is made
harder by the possibility that recovered pre-fire condition history is too sparse to baseline on, which the
design answers by stating recovered-versus-fresh per channel and tuning only on channels with provable
history. The official investigation into the 2021 failure at CS Energy's Callide C4 unit found that a piece of rotor
shaft weighing more than two tonnes was thrown five metres across the turbine hall, which is the failure mode
that unwatched trend evidence ends in.

The practical cost is that anomalies surface as alarms without prescribed actions, the warranty engineer
reviews evidence that lives in parallel registers rather than the DMS, and the operator has no way to
distinguish a sick machine from a sick instrument, because channel health is not separated from process
alarms anywhere.

Design goals
The design puts four goals on the platform, each tied to a specific failure mode at the combined cycle plant.
The first is protection without interference: the platform reads the upgraded DCS, the rehabilitated 3500
vibration monitoring rack, and the new generator's rotor-winding detection and hydrogen-leakage systems,
and it never writes to any of them, because the existing trip philosophy is preserved and the DCS read path
must not degrade plant operations.
The second is detection ahead of the trip. On STG-1 bearing housings the design watches vibration in mm/s
RMS, with 2.3 mm/s RMS as the steady-state reading and a breach defined as an excursion above it toward
the Zone C condition that forces a turbine trip, recorded at 6.21 mm/s RMS in the staged scenario. Detection
has to run on anomaly detection over vibration, hydrogen, winding and process telemetry, not on thresholds
alone, because the rehabilitated unit's recovered history may be too sparse to baseline every channel.
The third is alert discipline. Alert flooding trains operators to ignore a platform, so the plan puts a phase gate
of 2 false alerts per week, curates every series into unit-checked form, and separates channel health from
process alarms on the operator surface.
The fourth is compliance from the first week. NEPRA Security of IT and OT Regulations 2022 bind a grid-
connected generation company, so the design runs domain separation, least privilege, five years of tamper-
evident logs and the quarterly PowerCERT reporting schedule from phase one rather than retrofitting an audit
trail later.

Scoping decisions that de-risked the design
Three decisions were taken early, and each one bought safety at a price we accepted. The first was the OT
boundary: a hardware one-way egress path with a DMZ OPC UA collector instead of a direct control-network
connection, with a signed zone-and-conduit diagram as a phase one deliverable. The cost is that the platform
is structurally incapable of commanding the DCS, so every action it produces must land with a person,
through the shift operator's alerts and the engineer's review queue, and the freshness of DCS context
depends on the read cadence rather than on a live bidirectional link.
The second was to commit to pretrained open-weight models with no training run at all. The cost is that we
cannot tune to this unit's specific signature: phase two thresholds tune only on channels with provable

recovered history, and the migration report states recovered-versus-fresh per channel so nobody baselines
on air.
The third was to fix every tier to the operator's own hardware inside the plant perimeter, since Pakistan has no
hyperscaler region and no managed cloud service is assumed anywhere. The cost is operational: spares and
model updates arrive on the site's own import cycle roughly 600 km from the port region, so the design runs
mirror-archive delivery as its unit of change control and sizes spares for a long import gap.

What we chose against
The decisions in this design were mostly made against named alternatives, and the reasoning matters as
much as the choices themselves. On the model tier, the anomaly role went to MOMENT-1, an MIT-licensed
open time-series foundation model that detects and classifies anomalies zero-shot from one weights set,
because this design needs anomaly detection rather than forecasting alone; the Apache forecasters on the
table were ruled out for exactly that reason. On the drafting role, IBM Granite 4.2 8B under Apache-2.0 was
chosen over Qwen3.8 to 27B as the smaller, licence-clean fit with real KV headroom on a 48 GB-class site
card.
Two larger shapes were ruled out wholesale. A managed cloud architecture was ruled out because Pakistan
has no hyperscaler region, so the design runs entirely on plant hardware. A direct control-network connection
to the DCS was ruled out because it degrades plant operations if it fails.
Out of scope entirely: the agentic work surface is offered, not committed, pending the engineer's
confirmation, and integration with the plant CMMS or EAM stays unconfirmed with no price weight until it is.
Neither is a gap, because the alert and work-order path is complete without them and both can be added
once confirmed. The table below sets out each option, the decision taken, and the reason this operation ruled
it out.

The condition object model
The platform does not store turbine telemetry as documents in a basket. It holds ten object types taken from
the object model this engagement builds for the operator, and the design draws them as a graph. The
condition-bearing assets, the rehabilitated STG-1 and the new 280 MW 20 kV hydrogen-cooled STG, sit at
the centre. Around them sit the 3500 Vibration Monitoring Rack, Condition Anomaly Alert, Condition Work
Order, Instrument Calibration Record, Commissioning and Performance Test Record, the Shift Operator and
the Warranty Engineer, and an STG-1 Availability figure derived from the plant's real-time data. The links
between these objects are typed, so an alert is linked to the channel that raised it, the channel to the
calibration record that proves it was trustworthy, and the alert to the work order and the test record that close
it out.
This is what a query can reach that a document store cannot. Because the links carry types, the platform can
answer a question across objects in one traversal: show every vibration anomaly on STG-1 since the
rehabilitation, with the calibration state of each channel at the time it fired, and the work order and warranty
engineer now attached. In a document store that question becomes application code that joins loose records
by hand, and the joins rot.

Ingestion and the one-way event path
Eight named sources feed this platform: the upgraded plant DCS, the rehabilitated 3500 vibration monitoring
rack, the new generator's rotor winding short-circuit on-line detection device and hydrogen leakage
detectors, the fire detection instruments on the turbine bearing areas, the transformer diagnostic records, the
contract Document Management System, and the Primavera P6 programme. Four adapter families map them,
and the adapter tier is responsible for turning each source's native protocol and naming into instances of the
object model, so nothing downstream knows that a vibration channel arrived as an OPC UA node and a test
report arrived as a document.
The boundary hop is the one the design is most deliberate about. The DCS is read through a one-way OPC UA
path: a hardware one-way egress device with a DMZ OPC UA collector, so the platform reads process, alarm
and vibration context and can never write back, and the existing trip philosophy is untouched. The signed
zone-and-conduit diagram for this path is a phase one deliverable, and the NEPRA Security of IT and OT
Regulations 2022 require the firewalls and separation it documents. Timestamps come from a common time
reference, a PTP grandmaster running linuxptp, so a vibration sample, a DCS alarm and a camera frame can
be ordered against one another.
The streaming layer is responsible for the curated time-series layer: it receives adapter output, keeps the unit-
checked series the anomaly models consume, and separates channel health signals from process alarms so a
dead sensor is never mistaken for a sick bearing. Figure 7 shows how data moves, each named source into
the adapter family that maps it, the adapters into the one ontology core, and the core out to the surfaces a
person opens. Figure 8 shows the eight named systems mapped through the four adapter families, each row
carrying its provenance class, customer or domain-typical, because a domain-typical source such as the plant
CMMS carries no commitment until it is confirmed with the operator.

Inference at the plant edge

Every tier of this design runs on the operator's own hardware inside the plant perimeter. Pakistan has no
hyperscaler region, so no managed cloud service is assumed anywhere, and the plant sits roughly 600 km
from the port, so spares and model updates arrive on the site's own import cycle. The inference host is a 48
GB PCIe inference GPU class card on ruggedised edge servers, fed by hardened industrial switches, and the
network boundary is crossed by nothing: telemetry, models and alerts stay on plant, and the only scheduled
crossing is the mirror-archive delivery that carries updates inward on a controlled cadence.
The latency budget follows the two-loop discipline the domain brief set. The fast loop is the anomaly
detection on vibration, hydrogen, winding and process telemetry, which must classify a developing excursion
and raise a severity-ranked alert with a prescribed action to the shift operator faster than the operator's own
scan of the DCS would. The slow loop is the engineer's review queue, where diagnostic notes and test-report
drafts wait in the Document Management System for the warranty engineer during the defect liability period.
Both loops run on the same site card, which is why the model choice in the next section is sized to one card
rather than a cluster.
Figure 9 shows the hero workflow end to end: a bearing vibration excursion to Zone C forcing a turbine trip,
from the reading that carries it to the recovery written back to the ledger. At steady state the design holds
STG-1 bearing housing vibration at its nominal 2.3 mm/s RMS, and the staged fault drives it to 6.21 mm/s RMS
with the asset named and ringed. Figure 10 shows the camera wall at that moment, four feeds with the
detections drawn on them and the event stream alongside. When the link or the power is not there, the
platform does not go quiet. It reports through positive heartbeat and freshness indicators, with tested
degraded modes on the operator surface, so its own failure is visible rather than silent.

Two models, one card
The design runs two models, and both are pretrained open-weight models needing no training run, which is
itself a constraint of the site: with the plant roughly 600 km from the port and updates arriving on the import
cycle, a design that required a supervised training run on recovered history would be a design that could not
be maintained. Figure 11 shows the three-layer stack these two models sit in.
The first model is MOMENT-1, an MIT-licensed open time-series foundation model that performs anomaly
detection and classification zero-shot from one set of weights. It watches vibration, hydrogen, winding and
process telemetry. We chose it over the Apache-licensed forecasters because this design needs anomaly
detection, not forecasting alone, and because it is small enough to run on the 48 GB-class site card alongside
everything else. The second is IBM Granite 4.2 8B, Apache-2.0 with an enterprise vendor behind it, which
drafts the diagnostic notes and test reports the warranty engineer reviews. It was chosen over Qwen3.8 to
27B as the smaller, licence-clean fit for the same card, with real KV cache headroom left over.
The licences are a design constraint, not a footnote. The NEPRA Security of IT and OT Regulations 2022 bind
this platform to the operator's own hardware and audit trail, so every weight set on the card must be
redistributable, auditable and updatable through the mirror-archive unit of change control. Both models were
verified as available under their stated licences before the design was written, and neither requires a licence

key that phones home. The table below carries the full set of choices, the role each model holds and the

What degrades, and what must not
The design treats its own failure modes as first-class requirements, because a monitoring platform that fails
silently is worse than one that is not installed. The 2021 Callide C4 failure is the shape of the risk: the official

investigation report records a piece of rotor shaft weighing more than two tonnes thrown five metres across
the turbine hall. Nothing in this design assumes an operator will catch that with a round of the plant.
The named failures and their answers are as follows. If the DCS read path is built as a direct control-network
connection it can degrade plant operations, so the design puts a hardware one-way egress device with a DMZ
OPC UA collector in the path and reads the DCS without ever writing to it, preserving the existing trip
philosophy. If recovered pre-fire condition history is too sparse to baseline on, threshold tuning would quietly
rest on sand, so the migration report states recovered-versus-fresh per channel and phase two thresholds
tune only on channels with provable history. If alert flooding trains operators to ignore the platform, it fails in
the worst way, so the design carries a gate of 2 false alerts per week, curated unit-checked series, and
channel health separated from process alarms. If the audit trail is retrofitted, the five-year log and quarterly
PowerCERT duties are breached, so tamper-evident logs are wired from phase one.

How the design was reasoned
The method ran in layers, and the gaps shaped the design as much as the findings. The domain brief was the
primary input: it supplied the asset-to-alert-to-work-order pattern, the one-way DCS read rule and the two-
loop latency discipline, and its pitfalls P1, P2 and P3 shaped the OT boundary, the curated time-series layer
and the DMS write-back. No reference architecture was assigned to this domain, so the design proceeds on
the brief alone, stated as such rather than dressed up. From published work, Azure's Industrial IoT OPC UA
architecture contributed only its patterns, OPC UA subscriptions, imported asset models and read-only agent
access, with no managed cloud assumed.
Two entries on the proven shelf were searched and neither bears on turbine condition monitoring, so the
proven column came back empty, and we say so. Commercial precedent was more useful: Augury's
prescriptive-alert shape and Avathon's turbine prediction, with its honest 5-of-7 catch rate, guided the alert
design more than any vendor claim of completeness. The regulatory lens was checked against the NEPRA
Security of IT and OT Regulations 2022 as they stand, which bound the design to domain separation, least
privilege, five-year logs and quarterly PowerCERT reporting, and the 2003 blackout history drove the
heartbeat and freshness requirements. The model choices were verified live against their licences. One
candidate, redhat, ai-disconnected, was dropped in validation and nothing in this design stands on it. Figure

Evaluation and rollout
Nothing in this design has been measured, and this section is written in the future tense deliberately. The
delivery plan runs in three phases: phase one with nine items, phase two with four, and phase three with two,
and each phase closes on a gate rather than a demonstration. Phase one's gate includes the signed zone-
and-conduit diagram for the DCS read path and tamper-evident logging wired to the five-year NEPRA
schedule from the first day, because these cannot be retrofitted. Phase two's gate includes the migration
report stating recovered-versus-fresh history per channel, and thresholds tuned only on channels with
provable history.
What the plan would measure is the quantity the plant already understands: STG-1 bearing housing vibration
amplitude in mm/s RMS, with a nominal of 2.3 and a Zone C breach at 6.21 that forces a turbine trip. Around
that primary signal, the gates would measure the alert quality the operators actually feel, held to 2 false alerts
per week, and the platform's own visibility through positive heartbeat and freshness indicators.
Commissioning and performance test records and instrument calibration records land in the Document
Management System, so the Employer and the Engineer audit the same evidence the platform reasons over,
and condition due dates reconcile with the Primavera P6 programme.
